landing.heading: Urban Model Platform
landing.subtitle: Browse models, run scenarios & explore results on the map. Sign in to see your models and scenarios.
landing.publicHint: Without signing in you only see publicly available models!

jobs.empty: No runs yet. Start a scenario and you will find it here.
jobs.error: The runs could not be loaded. Is the UMP API responding?
jobs.notFound: This run does not exist or belongs to another account.
jobs.cacheHint: An identical scenario returns the same run, including its earlier result. A new run needs different inputs.
jobs.resultError: The result could not be loaded.
jobs.noResult: There is no result for this run.
jobs.resultPending: The result appears here as soon as the run has finished.

users.error: The accounts could not be loaded: {msg}
users.ownAccount: Your own account cannot be disabled here.
users.disableText: {name} can no longer sign in and is signed out everywhere right away. Roles and runs are kept, and the account can be enabled again at any time.

roles.tokenHint: Changes apply to {name} after their next sign-in or token refresh.
roles.loadError: The roles could not be loaded: {msg}

create.usernameInvalid: 3 to 50 characters: lower case letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore
create.inviteHint: The person receives an email with a link to set their password and confirm their address. The link is valid for three days.
create.invited: Account {name} created, the invitation is on its way to {email}.
create.notInvited: Account {name} created, but the invitation could not be sent. You can send it again from the menu in the list.

processes.title: Model processes

processes.anonymousHint: Without signing in you only see public processes. Sign in to see role-based ones such as fixbike.

commons.title: Commons
commons.anonymousHint: Without logging in, you can view the models. Log in to build your own commons.
commons.lead: The catalog is open to everyone. Explore the UFC Commons.

run.selectHint: Select a process on the left to run it.

job.failed: the run failed without giving a reason

locked.signedIn: Running {modell} needs your account to be cleared for {anbieter}. Looking at it and at other runs stays possible.
locked.anonymous: Running {modell} requires you to sign in. Looking at it stays possible without an account.

footer.carriers: Urban Futures Collective · City Science Lab · funded by the Prototype Fund

start.keycloakHint: Signing in goes through Keycloak. You leave this page briefly and come back here afterwards.

blocked.heading: This needs you to be signed in
blocked.reason: This page belongs to your account. After signing in you land back where you were heading.

hero.heading: Let city models do the computing.
hero.lead: The Urban Model Platform brings simulation models from research and public administration together in one place. Pick a model, set the parameters, look at the result and take it as a file. No GIS installation of your own, no computing power of your own.
hero.accessHint: Browsing needs no account. Running a model needs you to be signed in.
hero.credit: growbike for Oelde, drawn from a real run. Based on OpenStreetMap data, ODbL.

choose.title: Pick a model
choose.body: The catalogue shows which models exist and what they compute. Browsing needs no account.

configure.title: Set the parameters
configure.body: The form comes from the model description. Leave a field empty and the model uses its own default.

take.title: Take the result
take.body: The result appears on the map and can be downloaded as a file, for QGIS for example.

models.heading: Models computing today
models.lead: The catalogue is open to everyone.

ai.heading: Two ways to work with an AI
ai.lead: UMP-X provides no language model and pays for none. You bring your own, in the chat on this site or in your own client.

chat.heading: Chat on this site
chat.body: The chat knows the catalogue and the models' parameters. It picks out a model, explains the inputs and fills the form in. You are the one who submits.
chat.hint: You enter the provider and the key yourself, and the key stays in your browser. Chatting needs you to be signed in.

mcp.heading: Your own AI client over MCP
mcp.body: MCP is an open standard that lets AI clients use tools from other providers. If you already have a client, connect it once, sign in with your account, and the models are there as tools.

ai.title: Chat with your own AI

connect.heading: Connect your own AI
connect.lead: UMP-X provides no language model. You connect yours, so the choice and the cost stay with you.
connect.modelHint: Model names change often, so this is free text. Your provider lists them in its overview.
connect.warnKey: The key is stored unencrypted in this browser. Anyone with access to it can read it.
connect.warnData: Your questions go to the provider you choose. You pay for them.
connect.warnScope: Use a key created for this purpose only, with a spending limit.
connect.mcp: Or connect the MCP server to your own AI client.

examples.what: Which models are there and what do they compute?

ai.placeholder: Ask about models, data or parameters …
ai.disclaimer: Answers can be wrong. The page only starts a run after you confirm it.

clearConfirm.title: Clear the chat?
clearConfirm.body: The conversation is gone afterwards. It lives in this tab only, we keep no copy.

tools.startedByYou: Starting happens in the form, by you.

signIn.title: Sign in to chat
signIn.body: The chat works with your account and your own AI access. Both need you to be signed in.

experimental.title: Experimental feature
experimental.body: Requests go to your provider and are billed there. We can neither predict nor limit how many tokens a conversation uses.

help.title: Help
help.lead: UMP-X provides no language model and pays for none. To use the platform with an AI you bring your own. There are two ways, and both carry exactly your rights: without signing in the open model, signed in whatever you are cleared for.

chat.heading: Chat on this site
chat.lead: You connect your own model, then the chat walks you through the catalogue.

provider.title: Choose a provider
provider.body: OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenRouter, plus any service that speaks the OpenAI shape. A model running on your own machine works too.

key.title: Enter your key
key.body: You get the key from your provider. It stays in this browser and never reaches our server. Use a key created for this purpose only, with a spending limit.

ask.title: Ask questions
ask.body: The chat knows the catalogue and the models' parameters. It prepares a run and fills the form; you send it off.

mcp.heading: Your own AI client over MCP
mcp.lead: MCP is an open standard that lets AI clients use tools from other providers. We tested it with Claude Desktop.

address.title: Enter the address in your client
address.body: In Claude Desktop under Settings, Connectors, “Add custom connector”. Other clients call it a server or a tool source.

signin.title: Sign in with your account
signin.body: The client sends you to the platform's sign-in once. After that it holds exactly your rights, nothing more.

use.title: Use the models as tools
use.body: The models appear in the client as tools. Starting runs, checking status and fetching results all happen from there.

mcp.notAWebsite: The address is not a web page. Opened in a browser it only shows an error, and that is correct: it is meant for programs, not for looking at.

map.notMappable: This result cannot be shown on a map. You can still download it.

geometry.searchError: The place search did not answer.

hint.Polygon: Click the map to set corners; double-click closes the area. Corners can be moved afterwards.
hint.LineString: Click the map to draw the line; double-click ends it.
hint.Point: Click the map to set points. Points can be moved afterwards.

prototype.title: Prototype with sample data
prototype.text: This page shows how contributing and verifying will work. The models are samples; nothing is saved or sent to a server. After a reload everything is back to the start.

legal.draftText: This text is not final and not legally reviewed. Marked passages are still missing.
legal.germanOnly: This page is only available in German.

contribute.title: Contribute models
contribute.intro: Submit models from your model server here. Once reviewed, they appear in Commons.
contribute.empty: You have not submitted any models yet.

new.title: New model
new.serverWhy: The server your model runs on. It has to speak OGC API Processes. Its name becomes the prefix of the model id.
new.name: Name
new.nameInvalid: Lower case letters, digits and dashes only, 2 to 63 characters
new.urlInvalid: Please give an address starting with https://
new.authWhy: How the platform signs in to your server. Credentials are stored encrypted and never shown again.
new.secretNote: The prototype neither stores nor sends credentials.
new.processesWhy: These processes are offered by the server. Each one you choose becomes a model of its own.
new.next: Next, fill in the model card for each model and submit it.

card.title: Model card
card.why: What OGC does not describe: what the model is for, where its limits are and under which licence it is published. Required in the main language, the other language is optional.
card.defaultLangHint: All texts must be filled in this language.

explain.draft: Not submitted yet. Fill in the model card and submit the model for review.
explain.submitted: Submitted. Waiting for someone to take over the review. Until then you can withdraw it.
explain.changes_requested: The review has a request. Update the model card and submit again.
explain.verified: Reviewed and confirmed. It will be published soon.
explain.published: Published and visible in Commons. Changes to the model card apply right away.
explain.deactivated: Deactivated. New runs are not possible.

verifyExplain.submitted: Waiting for review. Take over the review to decide.
verifyExplain.in_review: Check model card and interface, start a test run and decide.
verifyExplain.changes_requested: Changes requested. Waiting for the provider.
verifyExplain.published: Published. If the interface changes, the review can be reopened.

facts.title: Technical details
facts.noInputs: Not read from the server yet.

verify.title: Verify models
verify.intro: Review, confirm and publish submitted models. Your own models are always reviewed by someone else.
verify.ownModel: This is your own model. Someone else has to review and publish it.
verify.testRunNote: Test runs are not possible in the prototype. Later, reviewers start a run here, also before the model is published.
verify.publishNote: On publishing, UMP-X creates the access role {role} in Keycloak.
